Putting an appliance under change control

How change requests gate destructive work on FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator — from the pre-upgrade run to an approved window — and exactly which paths are gated today.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage appliances.apply
📍 WhereAppliances → (a device) → Upgrade Preparation / Upgrade / HA failover; Automation → Change Requests

Overview#

Change control in SATOM means: a destructive change to an appliance needs an approved change request that names the appliance, and it may only run while the clock is inside that change's maintenance window. This covers all four products — FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator — and every console: open Change Requests from any ADOM and the device list shows what that ADOM can see (Global sees all), each device labelled with its product.

  1. 1Upgrade PreparationRun the pre-flight on the appliance; the run is stored
  2. 2Raise change requestOpens the change form with appliance, action and run pre-filled
  3. 3Window & rollbackFill the window (your timezone) and rollback plan; Create draft
  4. 4ApprovePrint the document, collect approvals, Approve in SATOM
  5. 5Schedule or act by handSchedule the bound action, or act on the appliance page inside the window
  6. 6Closed from the outcomeThe change completes or fails with the real result

Which actions are change-controlled#

The Change type list is derived from the automation catalog: every action that acts on a device and is destructive or changes objects.

Change type Products Runs from the scheduler?
Upgrade preparation (backup + health) FortiWeb, FortiADC Yes
Firmware upgrade (FULL - flashes + reboots) FortiWeb Gated, but does not flash (see below)
Reboot the appliance (DESTRUCTIVE) listed for all four; implemented for FortiWeb Yes, only bound to an approved change
HA failover - hand the primary role over (DISRUPTIVE) FortiWeb (firmware 8.0.0 or later), FortiADC (7.6.0 or later); one appliance Yes, only bound to an approved change
Cert Manager — lifecycle sweep (revoke + cleanup) FortiWeb Yes, only bound to an approved change
Custom REST call FortiWeb Yes, only bound to an approved change
Cert Manager — renew Server certs; renew Client+Server certs; renew Client certs FortiWeb Yes
Enable / disable a server policy; Enable / disable a backend (pool member); Change a backend's IP / port; Swap a server-policy certificate FortiWeb, one appliance Yes
Types added under Administrator → Change Types as configured No — documentary, carried out by hand

If a selected device's product is not supported by the chosen type, the form refuses to save and names the devices, rather than creating a change that would resolve to no targets.

Reboot is destructive and one-shot. It refuses to fire unless bound to an approved change inside its window. On a product other than FortiWeb it fails with ": reboot is not implemented for - no reboot endpoint has been verified against a live device of this product. NOTHING was sent to the appliance." A successful call means the box accepted the reboot — return to service is not confirmed by that call.

HA failover runs the product's CLI over SSH (there is no REST call for it) and refuses a FortiWeb below 8.0.0 by name, an appliance whose running firmware is not recorded, and a cluster member that is not currently reporting primary.

What is gated, and where#

Path Gate
Scheduled action bound to a change (created by Schedule) Re-checked at fire time: approved, external approval if required, inside the window. Refused fires are recorded as skipped and leave the change untouched
Upgrade, reboot, HA failover, Cert Manager lifecycle sweep or Custom REST call created by hand on Automations (no change bound) Refused: "… refused - this action runs only bound to an approved change request inside its window." The form cannot set or remove the binding; only the change's Schedule button writes it
Scheduled action bound to a change that does not cover it (another action, a device the change does not name, or the whole fleet when the change names devices) Skipped with the reason — "change request #N authorizes 'X', not 'Y'", "change request #N does not cover device id(s) …" or "change request #N authorizes named devices; this action targets the whole fleet". The change is left untouched
Schedule on a change that names no appliance Refused: "name at least one appliance before scheduling: an automated change runs only against the devices it names". The change can still be saved and read
Appliances → (device) → Upgrade, live push Needs an approved change of type Firmware upgrade naming the appliance, window open now
Appliances → (device) → Upgrade, dry run Not gated — nothing is sent to the appliance
Appliances → (device) → HA failover, live run Needs an approved change of type HA failover naming the appliance, window open now
satom execute device reboot|upgrade <device> --yes Fires the one existing scheduled action bound to an approved change for that single device; refuses ambiguity and fleet-wide rows
A Process step Actions that require a change request cannot be added to a process

The live Upgrade page (page, push, schedule and advisory), the boot-partition switch and the HA failover page need appliances.apply specifically; other edit permissions do not open them. Driving the change request itself needs users.manage.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: firmware upgrade, boot-partition switch and HA failover now require appliances.apply; before, any edit permission was enough. A live push or failover no longer closes a multi-appliance change after the first appliance: the change closes once every appliance it names has a result.

The live Upgrade page#

The page states which change authorises the push, or names the closest candidate and why it does not — for example before the maintenance window, change request is not approved or waiting for external change approval. A refused live push reports:

"Live upgrade refused — change control: . Run the upgrade preparation, raise a change request from it, get it approved, and flash inside its window."

When several approved changes qualify, the one whose window starts soonest is used. A live push additionally requires typing the exact appliance name. When an authorised push starts, its change moves to in progress.

Each live push (and each live HA failover) records that appliance's result on the change's timeline. A change that names one appliance closes at once as completed or failed. A change that names several stays in progress — and keeps authorising the remaining appliances inside its window — until every appliance it names has a result; it then closes as completed when all succeeded, or failed naming the appliances that did not, and the end-of-window notice goes out. A failed appliance can be retried inside the window; its latest result counts. If the window ends before every appliance has a result, close the change with Mark completed or Mark failed.

⚠️Warning — The scheduled firmware upgrade does not flash in this release

A Firmware upgrade action that fires from the scheduler inside an approved window reports "Firmware upgrade for is not executed by the headless service layer (no upgrade runbook); no firmware was flashed." and closes the change as failed. The change page of an open firmware-upgrade change shows the badge Flashed live, not by the scheduler. Use Schedule for the other change types; for firmware, flash from each appliance's Upgrade page inside the window.

The maintenance window is in your timezone#

The change form's Window start and Window end are read in the timezone set under Settings → General — the label next to each field names it — and stored as UTC. A value pasted with an explicit offset (for example 2026-08-10T22:00+00:00) is taken exactly as written.

For scheduled actions, daily, weekly and monthly times are also local wall-clock times, so "every night at 02:00" stays at 02:00 across daylight-saving changes; interval schedules are durations. The Once → Run at field of the scheduled-action form is read in the same console timezone (its label names the zone) and stored as UTC.

From pre-upgrade to change request#

Appliances → (a device) → Upgrade Preparation records every run: who ran it, the firmware at the time, the verdict and how many published services were captured. A finished run offers Raise change request, which opens the change form with the appliance, the action and that run selected.

Grading rules:

  • A section you did not tick cannot fail the run.
  • A published service that does not answer is a baseline, not a failure.
  • The run fails on: a failed backup, a failed health capture, a service sweep that could not enumerate the services at all, or an account without maintenance permission.

Runs are never overwritten; a re-run is a new record. A change may only cite runs of the appliances it targets.

The affected-service list is frozen#

The published services a change takes offline are captured onto it when it is raised (from the cited runs, merged, or from a live read). The detail page, the document and the exports read that capture, not the appliances as they are now. Compare against the devices now reports drift without merging it.

Each product contributes its own shape: server policies on FortiWeb, virtual servers on FortiADC. FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator publish no such object and contribute no rows.

Exporting the affected services#

Under the frozen list, tick the columns and press Download .xlsx or .csv. Fourteen columns are available: Device, Product, Management host, Policy / virtual server, Virtual server / interface, Service / port, Admin status, Probed URL, Reachable, HTTP status, Response (ms), Server pool, Backends, Note. The default selection is Device, Policy / virtual server, Virtual server / interface, Service / port, Admin status. Column order is fixed regardless of what you tick, and ticking nothing exports the default five.

The formal change document#

Every change prints a 13-section document: general information, purpose, affected systems, justification, impact, risk analysis, rollback plan, prerequisites, work to be performed, post-change validation, communication plan, approvals, outcome. View it in the browser or download it as Markdown, in English or German (other languages appear once their change-document text has been translated and the language is offered on the install).

  • The wording depends on the change type; a custom REST change prints the literal method, endpoint and body.
  • §8 (prerequisites) is filled from the cited pre-upgrade runs.
  • §12 prints the approval SATOM recorded and leaves other roles blank for signature.
  • §13 is filled once the change is closed.
  • Missing values print not recorded / nicht erfasst.

Troubleshooting#

"Live upgrade refused — change control: no approved change request names this appliance for upgrade."#

Solution — raise a change of type Firmware upgrade that includes the appliance, approve it, and push inside its window. A dry run does not need one.

The second appliance of my change cannot be flashed#

Possible causes — the window has ended, or the change was closed (by hand, by cancelling it, or because every appliance it names already has a result).

Solution — open the change and check its status and window. While it is in progress inside its window, the remaining appliances can still be flashed; otherwise raise a new change request for them.

My scheduled upgrade "failed" without touching the appliance#

Possible causes — the scheduler's upgrade executor does not flash in this release.

Solution — flash from Appliances → (device) → Upgrade inside a new approved window.
